variants.text: I don't think having sex means you should move in. Those decisions get tied together because sex makes the relationship feel further along than it necessarily is. Housing can complicate that. But once you're sharing rent and a bed every night, leaving or even slowing down gets harder for reasons that have nothing to do with whether the relationship is good. I like deciding beforehand when we're going to sit down and ask whether this is still working.

I'd also try to make some real friends together. My friends are going to hear me first and hers are going to hear her first. That's normal; they're our friends. The problem is when every person around the relationship only knows one of us well. Then the first serious conflict turns into two teams arguing about two different relationships.

I can know fast that I want somebody. I can't know fast that I want to raise kids with her or grow old with her, because I haven't seen enough of her life yet. Those are different questions. So I try to notice when “I’m taking a chance on this person” has somehow become “this is the right person.” If nothing new happened between those two thoughts, I probably just got more attached.

I also keep doing my own reparenting and meditation. If I stop because being loved makes me feel fine, I'm just waiting for the relationship to become responsible for how I feel. That's exactly the dependence I'm trying not to create.

I can learn a lot by talking, but there's a point where more questions mostly teach me what the person says about themself. After that I need ordinary time. Ten profound conversations in one weekend may tell me we can have profound conversations. They don't tell me what she's like on a boring day, or when she's annoyed and doesn't have an answer prepared.

If I keep getting a little feeling that something is off, I don't have to call it intuition or assume it's right. I also don't have to talk myself out of it because everything else feels good. I can just slow down enough to ask what it's about. Maybe it disappears once I understand it. Maybe it doesn't.
